title: KKR Stumbles in IPL 2025 Opener Against RCB
mainText: IPL 2025 began on March 22 at a packed Eden Gardens, where Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) lost to Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) by 6 wickets. KKR scored 178/6 under cloudy skies, with Venkatesh Iyer’s 52 off 38 and a late 20 off 8 from Rinku Singh. RCB chased it in 18.3 overs, with Virat Kohli’s unbeaten 82 off 49 silencing the 60,000-strong crowd. KKR’s decision to rely on spin backfired—Varun Chakaravarthy gave 42 runs in 4 overs. Mohammed Siraj’s 3/28 exploited early swing. New captain Ajinkya Rahane’s 12 off 15 drew boos, signaling a tough start to KKR’s title defense. RCB’s NRR jumps, while KKR face pressure to adjust tactics before Rajasthan Royals.
author: Ravi Sharma

title: Ishan Kishan’s Ton Powers SRH to Victory
mainText: Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) crushed Rajasthan Royals (RR) by 45 runs on March 23 in Hyderabad’s balmy weather. Ishan Kishan’s 112 off 58—12 fours, 6 sixes—lit up a raucous crowd, pushing SRH to 214/4. Aiden Markram’s 35 off 20 added late impetus. RR faltered at 169/8, despite Sanju Samson’s 67 off 41. Pat Cummins’s tactical 2/19, bowling cutters, outfoxed RR’s middle order. Trent Boult’s 1/48 and 10 wides reflected RR’s sloppy day. Kishan’s ton, SRH’s first since 2023, puts him in Orange Cap contention and validates their auction splurge. RR’s NRR dips, and their pace attack needs sharper execution. SRH’s dominance hints at a repeat of last season’s final run.
author: Priya Menon

title: CSK Outclass MI in High-Scoring Thriller
mainText: Chennai Super Kings (CSK) beat Mumbai Indians (MI) by 7 runs on March 23 at a steamy Chepauk. CSK posted 198/5, with Ruturaj Gaikwad’s 88 off 54—his third fifty-plus score against MI—and MS Dhoni’s 15 off 6 cameo thrilling fans. MI reached 191/9, with Suryakumar Yadav’s 76 off 45 falling short. Noor Ahmad’s 4/32, including Hardik Pandya’s duck, stunned MI’s dugout. Jasprit Bumrah’s 2/38 showed fight, but MI’s tail couldn’t handle CSK’s spin trap. The humid night favored turn, and CSK’s tactical bowling shift paid off. This win lifts CSK’s NRR and rekindles their rivalry fire. MI’s loss exposes Pandya’s captaincy nerves, needing a fix before their next outing.
author: Arjun Patel

title: Ashutosh Sharma’s Heroics Seal DC’s Win Over LSG
mainText: Delhi Capitals (DC) snatched a one-wicket win over Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) on March 24 in Visakhapatnam’s humid air. LSG scored 209/6, with Nicholas Pooran’s 85 off 47 and KL Rahul’s 29 off 18 setting a steep target. DC were reeling at 65/5, but Ashutosh Sharma’s unbeaten 66 off 31—5 sixes—turned the tide amid roaring fans. Axar Patel’s 3/34, with clever sliders, contained LSG. Rishabh Pant’s duck on LSG debut drew gasps, while Ravi Bishnoi’s 0/48 bled runs. Dew aided DC’s chase, finishing in 19.3 overs. This boosts DC’s NRR and showcases Sharma’s clutch ability. LSG’s bowling wilted late, and their new setup faces early questions.
author: Sneha Gupta

title: Punjab Kings Edge GT in Ahmedabad Nail-Biter
mainText: Punjab Kings (PBKS) beat Gujarat Titans (GT) by 4 wickets on March 25 under Ahmedabad’s clear skies. GT posted 183/7, with Shubman Gill’s 64 off 43 and a quick 28 off 15 from Rahul Tewatia. Arshdeep Singh’s 3/29, targeting the stumps, rattled GT’s plans. PBKS chased it in 19.4 overs, with Shreyas Iyer’s unbeaten 97 off 58—9 fours, 3 sixes—earning a standing ovation. Rashid Khan’s 2/36 nearly swung it, but GT’s fielding lapses (2 drops) cost them. Iyer’s calm captaincy debut lifts PBKS’s NRR. GT’s middle order faltered again, a recurring issue from 2024, and their bowlers lacked bite late. PBKS look poised for a strong run.
author: Vikram Singh

title: RR’s Bowling Woes Exposed by SRH Firepower
mainText: Rajasthan Royals (RR) slumped to a 45-run loss against Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) on March 23 in Hyderabad’s evening breeze. SRH smashed 214/4, with Ishan Kishan’s 112 off 58—12 fours, 6 sixes—and Abhishek Sharma’s 30 off 17. RR limped to 169/8, with Sanju Samson’s 67 off 41 a lone fight. Pat Cummins’s 2/19 exploited RR’s hesitancy, while Avesh Khan’s 0/52 drew crowd jeers. RR’s 15 extras and Trent Boult’s wayward 1/48 highlighted their bowling chaos. SRH’s power-hitting, backed by a vocal home crowd, overwhelmed RR’s tactics. This NRR hit stings RR early, and their pace unit needs a reset. SRH’s statement win echoes their 2024 aggression.
author: Neha Kapoor

title: Kohli’s 82 Sets Tone for RCB’s Campaign
mainText: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) launched IPL 2025 with a 6-wicket win over Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) on March 22 at Eden Gardens. KKR scored 178/6 in overcast conditions, with Venkatesh Iyer’s 52 off 38 and Sunil Narine’s 18 off 10. Virat Kohli’s unbeaten 82 off 49—6 fours, 4 sixes—drove RCB home in 18.3 overs, delighting traveling fans. Rajat Patidar’s 34 off 22 supported well. Mohammed Siraj’s 3/28 swung the powerplay, while KKR’s Andre Russell leaked 0/40. Kohli’s intent silenced retirement talks, boosting RCB’s NRR. KKR’s bowling misfired, and new captain Ajinkya Rahane’s conservative approach drew flak. RCB’s sharp start hints at a redemption arc after years of near-misses.
author: Karan Desai

title: MI’s Batting Falters Despite Yadav’s 76
mainText: Mumbai Indians (MI) fell 7 runs short against Chennai Super Kings (CSK) on March 23 at a muggy Chepauk. CSK posted 198/5, with Ruturaj Gaikwad’s 88 off 54—7 fours, 4 sixes—and Ravindra Jadeja’s 22 off 12. MI ended at 191/9, with Suryakumar Yadav’s 76 off 45—5 sixes—keeping hopes alive. Noor Ahmad’s 4/32, dismissing Hardik Pandya for a duck, stunned MI’s bench. Jasprit Bumrah’s 2/38 fought back, but MI’s lower order buckled under CSK’s spin web. The sticky pitch favored turn, and CSK’s crowd roared approval. MI’s NRR dips, and Pandya’s captaincy faces heat after a tactical misstep. CSK’s win cements their fortress reputation.
author: Anita Rao

title: LSG’s Pooran Shines in Losing Cause
mainText: Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) lost a thriller to Delhi Capitals (DC) by one wicket on March 24 in Visakhapatnam’s misty night. LSG scored 209/6, with Nicholas Pooran’s 85 off 47—6 sixes—and Ayush Badoni’s 25 off 14. DC chased it in 19.3 overs, with Ashutosh Sharma’s unbeaten 66 off 31—5 sixes—stealing the show. Axar Patel’s 3/34 outsmarted LSG’s top order, but Rishabh Pant’s duck on debut hushed the crowd. Mohsin Khan’s 0/50 and 12 wides undid LSG’s effort. Dew made bowling tough, and LSG’s death overs imploded. DC’s NRR rises, while LSG’s loss questions their new captain KL Rahul’s calls. Pooran’s knock deserved better support.
author: Suresh Nair

title: Gill’s 64 Not Enough as GT Lose to PBKS

Gill’s knock lacked support, and GT’s middle order woes persist from last season. PBKS’s NRR climbs, and Iyer’s leadership shines. GT need a batting rethink fast.

title: Iyer’s 97 Guides PBKS to Tense Victory
